transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hello, doctor. Thank you for taking the time to see me today. I, um... I hope I'm explaining this right. 

I guess I came in because I just can't seem to shake this... this heavy feeling that I've completely failed. As a father, mostly, and just as a useful person in general. I know it probably sounds foolish to say out loud, and I'm sorry to lay that on you right away. It's just that it keeps looping in my head, over and over, until I start feeling like I don't really deserve much of a future. 

I try to push those thoughts away, I really do, but they've been pretty stubborn lately. Does that make sense? Is that the sort of thing you needed to know?
How long have you been experiencing these feelings of failure?

Well, um... I guess it's been about a month now. It started right around the time my daughter left for college out of state. 

I mean, it's completely normal to miss your kids when they leave home, right? Every parent goes through it. I probably shouldn't even be making such a big deal out of it... I'm sure you see people with much worse problems than empty nest syndrome. But, yes, it's been about a month. I hope that's the kind of timeline you were looking for?
Have you been enjoying activities or hobbies that you normally find pleasurable over the past month?

Well, um... I usually have a few things I really enjoy. I've always loved working on my model railway, and watching the Cubs games. My daughter and I used to really look forward to those games together. 

But... I guess lately I haven't been keeping up with them as much as I probably should. The trains are just sort of sitting half-built on the table right now. I keep telling myself I need to finish them, I really do. And even just turning on a game on the TV... I don't know, it just feels a bit pointless lately. 

I know I shouldn't let myself get so lazy about the things I enjoy, and I'm sure I'll snap out of this little slump soon. I'm sorry, I know that's not a very good excuse. Does that answer your question? I hope I'm giving you what you need to know.
Have you been feeling less interested in things you usually enjoy, beyond just not having the energy to do them?

Well, um... I guess so, yes. It's not just that I'm too tired to work on the trains or watch the games. It's more like... the feeling of looking forward to them is just gone. 

Like I said, the trains are just sitting there half-built, and I know I have the physical energy to sit at the table and glue some pieces together. It's not heavy lifting or anything. But when I look at them, I just... I don't feel that spark I used to get. And the Cubs games... even just pressing the button on the remote feels like too much effort for something that doesn't bring me any joy right now. 

I feel terrible admitting that, it sounds so ungrateful to not even enjoy a simple baseball game. I'm sure it's just a phase and my interest will come back. I hope I'm explaining the difference clearly enough? I want to make sure I'm giving you the right kind of information.
Have you been having any thoughts about harming yourself or wishing you were dead?

Well, um... I really don't want to alarm you, and I promise I wouldn't ever actually do anything to hurt myself. I know how awful that would be for my daughter. But... if I'm being completely honest, because I know you need the truth to do your job... I guess I have had a few passing thoughts lately that it would just be easier if I didn't wake up in the morning. 

It's probably just the stress talking, I'm sure. But it actually did scare me a little bit recently. I sort of caught myself going over all my finances and paperwork, almost like I was... well, getting things ready for someone else to take over. 

I know I shouldn't let my mind go to those dark places, and I'm really sorry if that sounds terrible. I don't want you to think I'm crazy or anything. Is it... is it somewhat normal to have thoughts like that when you're in a slump like this? I hope I'm not making you worry too much, I just want to make sure I'm answering your questions properly.
Have you noticed any changes in your weight over the past month?

Well, um... I suppose I might have lost a little bit of weight. Nothing to be too concerned about, I promise! I just... I've noticed I've had to tighten my belt a notch or two recently. 

I know I really should be taking better care of myself, and I feel a bit ashamed admitting this to a doctor, but most days lately I just don't bother making a real meal. I sort of just forget to eat entirely until it gets quite late, and by then, I usually only manage to have some toast or a bowl of cereal. 

I know that's a terrible habit, and I really am going to try to do better about cooking proper dinners for myself. I don't want you to think I'm completely neglecting my health. Does that answer your question? I hope I'm giving you the right kind of details.
Have you experienced any periods where these feelings of failure and lack of interest in activities lasted for a shorter time, say less than two weeks, before improving on their own?

Well, um... I've really been trying to snap out of it, I promise I have. But... no, I don't think I've had any time recently where it just went away on its own like that. It seems like this... this slump has just been sort of hanging over me continuously for quite a while now. 

I know I should be trying harder to push through it, and I'm honestly a bit embarrassed that I haven't been able to just shake it off after a few days like a normal person would. I really want to be making progress. I hope I'm understanding your question right? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the most helpful answers so you can do your evaluation properly.
Have you been experiencing any feelings of nervousness or anxiety lately?

Well, um... I really wouldn't say I've been overly anxious or anything like that. I mean, I know I mentioned being a bit stressed earlier, but it's nothing I can't handle, I promise. 

I don't want to sound like a hypochondriac or like I'm complaining about every little thing. I suppose I might have felt a tiny bit on edge here and there, just with everything going on, but... no, I wouldn't call it nervousness or anxiety. I'm generally pretty good at keeping my nerves in check. 

I hope that's okay? I just want to make sure I'm not making a big deal out of nothing. Is that the kind of information you were looking for?
Have you been feeling restless or sluggish lately?

Well, um... no, not really. I mean, I suppose I might be moving a little slower than usual, but I think that's just because I haven't been keeping as active as I should be. It's my own fault, really. I promise I'm not just lying around all day doing absolutely nothing. 

I try to keep myself busy with small things around the house, so I wouldn't say I'm sluggish, exactly. And I definitely haven't been restless or pacing around or anything like that. I'm usually pretty calm. 

I know I need to make more of an effort to get up and get moving, and I really am going to start doing that. I hope that makes sense? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right picture of how things are.
Have you had any difficulty concentrating or making decisions lately?

Well, um... I guess maybe a little bit? I mean, I don't want it to sound like I'm completely losing my mind or anything, I promise I'm not. I've always been really sharp with that kind of stuff. I used to manage these massive engineering spreadsheets at work without even having to think twice about it. 

But, well... lately, I suppose I have been having a bit of a hard time focusing. It's embarrassing, honestly. I'll just be sitting there staring at a simple grocery list, or trying to figure out a basic bill, and half an hour will go by and I just... I can't seem to decide what to do next. 

I know I just need to apply myself more, and I'm really trying to get back to my old self. I'm sure it's just a temporary thing, right? I hope I'm not making it sound worse than it is. Does that help answer your question?
Have you experienced any unusual thoughts or heard any voices that others couldn't hear?

Oh, goodness, no. Um... definitely nothing like that, I promise. 

I know I mentioned being a bit foggy and having trouble with my focus earlier, but my mind is still very much my own. I'm certainly not... well, I'm not losing touch with reality or anything like that. I haven't heard any voices or had any bizarre thoughts. I'm completely normal in that department, I assure you. 

I hope that's a good thing? I just really want to make sure I'm giving you the right information and not making you worry that I'm completely falling apart. I'm still very grounded, I promise. Is that the answer you were hoping for?
Are there any activities that you still find pleasure in or look forward to?

Well, um... I mean, I really try to stay positive and keep up with my hobbies. I don't want you to think I'm just giving up on everything, because I'm not. I've always been a very active guy. 

I used to really love working on my model railway... it's this big layout I've been building for years. And watching the Cubs games with my daughter, that was always our special thing. But... well, I guess lately, I just haven't been as on top of it. 

It's silly, really. The trains are just sitting there half-built on the table right now. And even when a game is on TV, I just... I don't know, turning it on just feels a bit pointless lately. I'm sure it's just a phase, though! I just need to force myself to sit down and do it, right? I'm going to try harder to get back into it, I promise. Does that make sense? I hope I'm not sounding too negative.
Have you ever thought about how you would hurt yourself if you were to act on those thoughts of not waking up?

Oh, um... no, no, I would never actually do anything to hurt myself. I promise you that. I know how terrible that would be for my family, especially my daughter. I'm not that kind of person, I really aren't. 

It's just... well, like I said, sometimes my mind just wanders to this idea that it would be so much easier if I just... slipped away in my sleep. Just didn't wake up. It's just a fleeting thought, really! But... I guess I did do something a little silly the other day that sort of spooked me. 

I was looking over all my old financial spreadsheets, making sure everything was perfectly organized and clearly labeled... and I realized I was doing it so that it would be easy for someone else to take over if I wasn't around. It really scared me when I caught myself doing that. I stopped right away, of course. 

I know that sounds bad, but it was just a moment of weakness. I'm not making any actual plans or anything like that, I swear. I'm safe, I promise. Is it okay that I told you that? I don't want you to think I'm a danger to myself or anything.
Have you ever felt this way before, with these same kinds of thoughts and feelings, at any other point in your life?

Oh, um... no. No, never anything like this. I promise you, I've always been a very, um, steady person. Very reliable. 

I mean, everyone has their off days or feels a little stressed sometimes, right? But I've never had these kinds of... well, these dark thoughts, or this much trouble just getting through a normal day. I've always been very capable. I got my degree, I always took care of my responsibilities... I've never been the type of guy to just let things slide or fall apart. 

So this is all completely new for me. I really hope you don't think I've been hiding a long history of this from you or anything like that. I'm usually very put-together, I swear. I'm sorry if that doesn't give you much background to work with... is it okay that this is the first time it's happened? I just really want to make sure I'm giving you the answers you need to figure this out.
Have your feelings of failure and lack of interest in activities lasted for most of the day, nearly every day, for the past two weeks?

Well, um... I guess if I'm being completely honest, yes. It's been most of the day, pretty much every day. But really, it's only been going on for about a month! It's not like I've been like this forever. 

It all sort of started when my daughter left for college out of state. I mean, it's a huge adjustment, right? Any parent would feel a little lost when their kid moves away. So it makes sense that I'd be a little down and out of sorts for a bit. I'm sure I just haven't figured out my new routine yet. 

I really don't want you to think I'm just wallowing in it all day. I do try to keep busy and shake it off. But yeah, for the last month or so, it's just been a bit harder to shake than I expected. Is that a normal reaction to have? I hope I'm not overreacting to her leaving. I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right picture of how long this has been happening.
Have you had any episodes like this before in your life, where you felt similar feelings of failure and lack of interest in activities?

Oh, um... no. Like I think I mentioned just a little bit ago, I really haven't. I've never had a time in my life where I felt like this before. 

I've always been a pretty driven person, you know? I always took a lot of pride in what I did, and I certainly never felt like a... well, like a failure, until recently. And I always really enjoyed my hobbies and keeping active. So, no, there weren't any past times like this at all. 

I'm sorry if that makes it harder for you to figure out what's going on with me. I know sometimes having a history or a pattern helps doctors piece things together, right? I hope it's okay that this is all just brand new to me. I just really want to make sure I'm being helpful and answering your questions the right way. Am I doing okay with all this?
Are there any activities that you still find pleasure in or look forward to, even if it's just a little bit?

Well, um... I really try to find things to enjoy, I promise I do. I know it's important to stay active. But, um... to be completely honest, it's been really hard lately to get excited about much of anything. 

I used to really love working on my model railway, you know? It was this big project I was so proud of. And I always looked forward to watching the Cubs games, especially with my daughter before she left. But now... well, the trains are just sitting there on the table, half-built. I haven't touched them in weeks. And even just turning on the TV to catch a game... it just feels sort of pointless right now. I just can't seem to care who wins or loses anymore. 

I feel terrible saying that, because I know I should be keeping up with my hobbies. I really hope you don't think I'm just giving up or being lazy. I want to enjoy those things again, I really do. I'm sorry, I know that's probably not the answer you were hoping for. Is it normal to lose interest in things you used to love this much? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.
Do you feel like these feelings of failure and lack of interest are interfering with your daily life and relationships?

Well, um... I guess I'd have to say yes, it is starting to interfere a bit. I mean, I try really hard to keep on top of things, I really do. But... well, my bills and some of the house projects I started are kind of piling up on me. I just... I sit down to do them and I can't seem to make myself follow through. I always used to be so organized, so it's a little embarrassing to admit that things are slipping. 

And, um, socially... I guess I've pulled back a little. I used to go to a book club, and I'd go on bike rides with a few guys I know, but I've sort of stopped seeing them lately. I just haven't had the energy to keep up appearances, I suppose. I hope that doesn't make me sound like a bad friend. I'm sure they understand I'm just going through a phase.

But, um... I guess the part that really made me realize I couldn't just brush this off anymore is... well, I started organizing my finances. But, like, organizing them in a way... like someone else might need to take over them. I don't know why I did that, it just felt like something I should do. 

I'm sorry, I know that sounds a bit alarming. I promise I'm not trying to be dramatic. I just want to make sure I'm giving you the full picture so you can help me. Is it okay that I shared that? I just want to make sure I'm doing this right.
Have you had more than one episode of feeling this way in your life?

Oh, um... no. Just this one time. I know we touched on this a little bit earlier, and I am so sorry if my answer back then was confusing at all. I really try to be clear. But, no, I haven't had more than one. This is the very first time in my life I've ever felt this way. 

I've never had a past episode or anything like that before this started. I hope I'm not frustrating you by not having a longer history for you to look at, I know that probably makes it trickier to figure me out. Is this all making sense the way I'm explaining it? I just want to be as helpful as I can.
